## Analysis: Was the Claim That Red No. 3's Removal "Was Not Final and Might Never Take Effect" a Fair Reading in Mid-2025?

### The Procedural Context in Mid-2025

The January 2025 order (90 FR 4628) revoked the color additive listings for FD&C Red No. 3 in food (§ 74.303, effective January 15, 2027) and ingested drugs (§ 74.1303, effective January 18, 2028). However, under sections 701(e)(2) and 721(d) of the FD&C Act, the filing of objections **automatically stayed** the effectiveness of the order. As the later document confirms:

> "Under sections 701(e)(2) and 721(d) of the FD&C Act, the filing of objections operates to stay automatically the effectiveness of our repeal of §§ 74.303 and 74.1303 until we take final action on the objections." [91 FR 50475 (V. Summary and Conclusions)]

Objections were filed by the February 18, 2025 deadline. This means that during mid-2025, the January 2025 order was indeed **under an automatic administrative stay**. It was technically not yet "final" in the sense that the agency had not completed its evaluation of objections, and the effective dates were suspended pending that resolution.

### Was It a "Fair Reading"?

**Partially fair, but overstated.** It was accurate to say in mid-2025 that:

- The order was under an automatic administrative stay.
- FDA had not yet issued its final action on the objections.
- The effective dates were suspended.

However, saying it "might never take effect" was a stretch. The January 2025 order was grounded in the **Delaney Clause**, which operates as a matter of law once the factual predicate (inducing cancer in laboratory animals) is established. FDA explicitly found that "FD&C Red No. 3 has been shown to cause cancer in laboratory animals" and that "under the Delaney Clause this finding of carcinogenicity renders the color additive 'unsafe' as a matter of law" [90 FR 4628 (VI. Conclusion)]. The Delaney Clause leaves FDA no discretion: a color additive found to induce cancer "shall be deemed unsafe, and shall not be listed" [91 FR 50475 (B. Objection 2)]. Given this mandatory legal framework, the realistic prospect of the order being permanently revoked through the objection process was slim—the objectors would have needed to undermine the factual finding of carcinogenicity itself, not merely argue about safety at intended use levels.

### The Position Now

The later document (91 FR 50475) resolves the matter definitively:

> "We have completed our evaluation of the objections and conclude that a continuation of the administrative stay of the effective dates for the repeal of §§ 74.303 and 74.1303 is not warranted."

> "Therefore, we are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective **January 15, 2027**, and **January 18, 2028**, respectively."

FDA overruled all objections, denied requests for a public hearing, and confirmed the original effective dates. The agency emphasized that it "does not have discretion to list a color additive determined to be safe under the general safety clause if it is found to induce cancer under the Delaney Clause" [91 FR 50475 (B. Objection 2)].

### Conclusion

The mid-2025 characterization that the removal "was not final" was **technically correct** at that moment—the automatic stay was in effect and FDA had not yet ruled on objections. But the claim that it "might never take effect" was **not a fair reading** of the legal landscape, because the Delaney Clause is mandatory and non-discretionary once the cancer finding is made, leaving objectors with an extremely narrow path to reversal. The current position is that the stay has been lifted, the objections have been overruled, and the ban will take effect on the originally scheduled dates.

## CFR Provisions Changed by the Red No. 3 Order

The January 2025 order affects two CFR provisions, and they do **not** all change on the same day:

### 1. **§ 74.303** (Use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food, including dietary supplements)
- **Action:** Removed/revoked — the regulation will no longer provide for the safe use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food.
- **Effective date:** January 15, 2027

### 2. **§ 74.1303** (Use of FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs)
- **Action:** Removed/revoked — the regulation will no longer provide for the safe use of FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs.
- **Effective date:** January 18, 2028

### Additional Interim Amendment to § 74.1303
Because § 74.303 is removed first (2027) while § 74.1303 remains in effect until 2028, the order also **amends § 74.1303** to incorporate the identity and specifications language from § 74.303(a)(1) and (b) directly into § 74.1303(a). This is necessary because § 74.1303 previously cross-referenced § 74.303 for those details, and that cross-reference would become invalid once § 74.303 is removed. This interim amendment takes effect on the same date § 74.303 is removed (January 15, 2027).

### Summary
The two removals occur on **different dates** — approximately one year apart — giving food manufacturers two years and ingested drug manufacturers three years to reformulate.
